key_insight: Iterative strong coupling stabilizes FD-SPH simulations of lightweight floating bodies where single-pass coupling fails, even with drastically smaller time steps.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports simulation of lightweight, complex-shaped floating bodies in transient free-surface flows without explicit interface reconstruction or surface-normal evaluation.
method: Combine volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton–Euler rigid-body updates.
Iteratively feed back the velocity mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious fluid and the rigid body within each time step.
Compare single-pass and iterative coupling under matched conditions.
evidence_signal: Tests include a settling disk, buoyant cubes, wet-bed dam breaks and star-shaped bodies; iterative coupling remains stable across tested specific gravities of 0.1–1.0, while single-pass coupling fails at 0.1 and 0.2.
watch_item: All reported production runs meet the coupling-residual tolerance, but computational cost and stability beyond the tested conditions remain unquantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
